title: Get property details structuredContent
description: The `structuredContent` of the `get_property_details` MCP tool: one property, everything the T-02 inline card and full-screen page render. Base: PRD T-02 section 6.1 'Illustrative data packet — canonical output', field names verbatim (snake_case, nested as in the packet). On top of the PRD, the additions the built widget needs, each marked 'ADDED' in its description: `brand_code` and `nearby[]` (same meaning as T-01), `pricing.availability_status` / `next_available_date` (T-01's on-request handling), `reviews.individual_reviews` as a real array (PRD OQ-02 placeholder), `asset_base_url`, and two UI-only optional blocks the PRD does not have: `accessibility_note`, `awards` (user decision 2026-10-10). Left out: `pet_policy` (the client has no such data, 2026-10-15) and the PRD's `points_of_interest` placeholder (replaced by `nearby[]`). `best_rate_guaranteed` was a PARAMETER GAP and is accepted since 0.3.0. `services[]` was removed in 0.4.0: the 'Rooms and services' cards are the same on every property (text and image), so the widget holds them. 0.5.0 adds the optional `location.city`, `location.country` and `location.country_code` (the property page link). 0.5.0, provisional (2026-10-18).

property_code.description: PRD `propertyCode`, e.g. "50926". The same code as T-01's `property_code`.

brand_code.description: ADDED (same as T-01). The upstream `brand` slug, passed through verbatim, e.g. "ascott-the-residence". The widget maps it to its bundled brand lockup and colour; `brand_name` is display text only. See find-properties/README.md §1.

brand_name.description: PRD `brandName`, display text, e.g. "Ascott The Residence".

brand_logo_url.description: PRD `brandlogo`: upstream path or URL; "" when there is none. A fallback only: the widget prefers its bundled lockup for `brand_code`.

banner_image_url.description: PRD `bannerImageMobile`: the hero image. Upstream path, resolved by the widget against `asset_base_url`. Optional: many properties have none.

thumbnail_url.description: PRD `newPropertyThumbnail`. Required: the hero falls back to it when `gallery` and `banner_image_url` are absent (EC partial data).

email.description: PRD `email`. Shown in the full-screen header.

phone.description: PRD `phone` (bookingsearchresultv2, else getpropertyinfo). Shown in the full-screen header.

tags.description: PRD `tag[]`. The widget shows the titles of tags with `propertyTagPresent: true` as chips (inline card). Plain titles, no emoji.

items.description: One tag chip. Field names are the PRD packet's, camelCase as written there.

description.description: PRD `description`: CMS HTML (the PRD's type is 'String (HTML)'). The widget renders it as plain text, stripping tags; it never injects HTML.

gallery.description: PRD `gallery[]` → path, gallery_image, gallery_type, title. The hero carousel. Optional (partial data); when absent the hero uses `banner_image_url`, then `thumbnail_url`.

availability_status.description: ADDED (same as T-01). `available`: `per_night_rate_pref_curr` is required and shown. `on_request`: no rate is shown; `next_available_date` may say when it is bookable.

per_night_rate_pref_curr.description: PRD `perNightRatePrefCurr`, decimal string upstream, a number here. The 'from … / night' figure.

currency.description: PRD `currency`, ISO 4217. Every rate uses it. (T-01 calls the same field `currency_code`; the PRD packet names differ and each contract follows its own PRD.)

based_on.description: PRD `based_on`: the stay and guests the rates were quoted for, after server defaults.

checkin.description: The stay the rates are for.

city.description: ADDED 0.5.0, optional. Same as T-01 `properties[].location.city`. Not shown by the widget; for the model.

country.description: ADDED 0.5.0, optional. Same as T-01 `properties[].location.country`, e.g. "Singapore". Not shown by the widget; for the model.

country_code.description: ADDED 0.5.0, optional. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, upper case, e.g. "SG" (upstream `countryCode`). The widget builds the fullscreen "Open in" link to the property's page on discoverasr.com from it (`/{language}/{brand_code}/{country}/{property}`); without it the link falls back to the site's search.

local_address.description: PRD `localAddress` (getpropertyinfo), the localised address when it differs.

map_image_url.description: PRD `mapImage`: upstream static map image. Optional: the widget can draw the map from `coordinates`.

description.description: CMS HTML; rendered as plain text.
CMS HTML; rendered as plain text.
Label, e.g. "Pool". De-duplicated by the server (see find-properties/README.md §2).

imagePath.description: Upstream icon path. The widget's icon KEY is the file name ("icon-pool"); the image is never loaded (T-01 decision).

charge.description: e.g. "free", "paid". Optional: null on every website row.

facility_groups.description: The inline amenity row and the 'Property highlights' grid use the facilities of every group, in order. May be empty.

score_label.description: e.g. "Excellent". In the PRD packet, not in the §6 table; source to confirm.

items.description: One review card. ADDED shape: the PRD lists reviewer name, rating, date, source and text but no field names (OQ-02).

reviewer_name.description: e.g. "Andy Andrea"; the widget derives the avatar initials.

posted_date.description: The widget shows month and year ("Posted July 2027").

text.description: Review body; truncated by the card.

individual_reviews.description: ADDED as an array. The PRD packet has a string placeholder here ('PENDING OQ-02'). Optional: without it the Ratings & Reviews section shows the summary only.

hotel_information.description: PRD `hotel_information`. Every field optional (partial data); the widget shows a cell only for a field that is present, and hides the whole Hotel Information section when none is. Cell titles are the widget's own translated labels, not data. 0.3.0 (2026-10-15): `best_rate_guaranteed` added (was a PARAMETER GAP, PRD OQ-05). `pet_policy` (PRD AC-08 / OQ-04) is deliberately NOT accepted: the client has no pet policy data (user decision 2026-10-15).

check_in_time.description: PRD `checkInTime`, 24-hour "15:00:00". The widget formats it for the locale.

title.description: e.g. "Language(s) our staff speak". Accepted for compatibility but NOT shown since 0.3.0: the cell title is the widget's translated label, so it follows the user's language.

cancellation_policy.description: PRD `cancellationPolicy`, CMS HTML, rendered as plain text. The 'Cancellation and Pre-payment' cell.

best_rate_guaranteed.description: ADDED 0.3.0 (2026-10-15, user decision): the Best Rate Guaranteed text, plain text, e.g. "Applicable under property's Terms and conditions". Shown as the value under the widget's 'Best Rate Guaranteed' title; absent = no cell. PRD OQ-05: source to be confirmed by MuleSoft. Sent in the language of the response, not translated by the widget.
examples: Applicable under property's Terms and conditions

nearby.description: ADDED (same as T-01 `nearby[]`, same POI source). Replaces the PRD's `points_of_interest` placeholder (API GAP, OQ-07): up to 5 POIs for 'What's nearby?'.

asset_base_url.description: ADDED (T-01 has it as `meta.asset_base_url`). Origin the widget resolves relative image paths against; default https://www.discoverasr.com.

accessibility_note.description: ADDED, UI-only (user decision 2026-10-10): the 'Accessible Property' note under Hotel Information (Figma 1495:12026). Not in the PRD; field name ours; MuleSoft to find a source.

awards.description: ADDED, UI-only (user decision 2026-10-10): the mobile AWARDS strip (Figma 572:54916). Not in the PRD; field name ours.

coordinates.description: Copied verbatim from contracts/find-properties/structured-content.ui.schema.json `$defs`, so a POI / image / coordinate means the same thing in T-01 and T-02. Change both together. Required in both versions and genuinely needed, but note the gap is on OUR side: `PropertyCardVM` carries no latitude/longitude, so the preview scatters pins at hard-coded percentages (FindPropertiesView.tsx:174). Wiring the real Google Map means adding these to the view model — nothing is missing from the contract.

path.description: The image the carousel renders. Upstream path verbatim, resolved like every image field (see `meta.asset_base_url`).

gallery_type.description: Not consumed. Required in 0.1.0; kept so the two versions stay comparable.

title.description: Used as the slide's alt text, falling back to `property_name`.

galleryImage.description: Copied verbatim from contracts/find-properties/structured-content.ui.schema.json `$defs`, so a POI / image / coordinate means the same thing in T-01 and T-02. Change both together.

pointOfInterest.description: Copied verbatim from contracts/find-properties/structured-content.ui.schema.json `$defs`, so a POI / image / coordinate means the same thing in T-01 and T-02. Change both together. One point of interest near a property, feeding both POI surfaces: the panel row and the map callout. REWRITTEN to mirror the real upstream shape — the ODX `pois[]` array that MuleSoft will call, supplied by the customer 2026-10-01. Before that it was modelled from the preview fixture, which turned out to be both poorer (no id, category, type or distance) and richer (a prose `description` and an `emoji` that ODX does not have) than the real thing. Field names are snake_case here rather than ODX's camelCase, and `coordinates` is a nested object of NUMBERS rather than two top-level strings, because both are already this contract's house style and splitting it per-field would leave one response internally inconsistent — property coordinates nested numbers, POI coordinates flat strings. The per-field provenance below is the mapping specification for MuleSoft. Note that ODX also supplies `distanceMetres`, which this schema deliberately does NOT accept — the only place in either contract where an available upstream field is refused rather than passed through; see find-properties/README.md for the decision and its one consequence.

poi_id.description: ODX `poiId`, e.g. "poi-50926-01". The stable identity: React key for the panel row, selection id for the callout. Note the value is namespaced by the property code — `50926` is this property's `property_code` — which is independent evidence that ODX treats POIs as belonging to a property rather than to the search area, and so corroborates modelling them per property rather than response-level.

title.description: ODX `poiName`. Named `title` and not `label` — which is what `PropertyNearbyPOI` calls it — on two grounds: `MapCallout`'s own prop is `title`, and "label" is UI vocabulary describing where a string is painted rather than what it is. A data contract should name the thing. The view-side rename is listed in find-properties/README.md.

category.description: ODX `poiCategory`, the coarse tier of a two-level taxonomy. Confirmed to be the SAME taxonomy as the legend table pasted into the T-01 Figma frame (node 1006:60836), whose five observed categories are listed in `examples` below. Deliberately a plain string and NOT an `enum`, unlike `brand_code` — the legend is a rasterised image rather than a text node, so it cannot be transcribed with certainty, and it carries no Food or Dining category even though the design's own map callouts are restaurants and bars and `CategoryPin` ships a `Food` variant. Either the pasted table is partial or dining POIs arrive by another route; until that is answered, an enum would reject valid payloads. Tighten it to an enum once the taxonomy is confirmed complete.

type.description: ODX `poiType`, the fine tier. 21 values observed in the Figma legend: Theme park; Shopping mall, Boutique, Bookstore, Artisan market, Florist, Home goods; Spa, Gym, Yoga studio, Aquatics; Luxury hotel, Boutique hotel, Budget hotel, Resort; Park, Bridge, Temple, Heritage building, Beach, Viewpoint. Same reason as `category` for staying a string.

icon_code.description: ODX `iconCode`, which is an EMOJI (e.g. "🌳", "🛍️"), not a snake_case code — corrected 2026-10-03 when the customer supplied the upstream value list (mock-mcp/mock-data/poi_icon_code.json, 70 distinct). Pass it through verbatim; the widget renders it as the POI marker as-is. This retires the earlier plan of a widget-owned `icon_code` → emoji table keyed off the rasterised Figma legend: upstream already chooses the glyph. Deliberately no `pattern` or `enum`: emoji include variation selectors and multi-code-point sequences that a regex would have to enumerate, and a closed list written from one sample would reject valid payloads (the `brand_code` lesson). MuleSoft must NOT map it to a name.

coordinates.description: ODX `latitude` and `longitude`, which arrive as decimal STRINGS ("1.2876") and must be converted to numbers per this contract's normalization rule. Required: a POI is placed on the map exactly as a property pin is — `FindPropertiesView.tsx:185` states it, "At runtime the map projects them from POI coordinates" — and the preview only hides that because `CALLOUT_POSITIONS` drops two callouts at hard-coded percentages lifted from the Figma frame.

address.description: ODX `poiAddress`. Not consumed by any T-01 surface; kept because it costs nothing to pass through and the model may cite it in prose.

distance_minutes.description: ADDED 1.1.0 (T-01) / 0.2.0 (T-02), 2026-10-15, user decision: walking time from the property to this POI, in whole minutes. Optional: a POI without it is still shown, without a walk time. MuleSoft supplies the value already in minutes; the widget does not convert. Rendered as "- {n} mins walk" after the POI name (Figma T-02 inline 1630:41645). Upstream ODX has `distanceMetres` (metres, not minutes); how the minutes are derived is MuleSoft's to confirm.
